title: Conditional weighted recurrence yields distance decay, while the Q3 recurrence remains open
question: If the Q3 local commutator seminorms satisfy a volume-uniform nonnegative graph recurrence, does a spatially weighted norm imply a volume-uniform distance decay bound?
method: Use the induced nearest-neighbor boxes of side 3 and 5 with degree bound z=6 and exact weight exp(rho)=2.
Verify the weighted one-step inequality W(L_next)<= [1+(C+J z exp(rho)) delta]W(L) for C=J=1 and delta=1/5 in a SymPy/Fraction primary lane.
Iterate six steps and verify pointwise distance decay from the weighted norm, with the same constant on both box sizes.
Compile Lean R210 for the scalar split-factor, positive-weight pointwise and recurrence identities.
Keep the EXP-001025 locality separation and the QFT-to-TECT production firewall; do not treat the conditional recurrence as an actual Q3 theorem.
finding: Primary 20/20, independent 20/20, integrated 25/25 and Lean R210 pass. Under the explicit nonnegative local graph recurrence, the weighted norm obeys W_rho(L_N)<=exp((C+J z exp(rho))T)W_rho(L_0), hence L_x(T)<=exp(-rho d(x,X)+(C+J z exp(rho))T)W_rho(L_0), with constants independent of finite-box volume. The exact Q3 onsite-plus-bond flow has not been shown to satisfy the required recurrence.
decision_reason: This closes only the conditional recurrence-to-decay bridge and identifies the actual missing Q3 analytic statement. It does not close first-passage resummation, boundary commutator decay, exhaustion Cauchy, common alpha or KMS.
